scope: First visual-review batch for observed response features in real ACN development histories. No algorithm fit, parameter search or held-out test access in this batch.
source: data/ACN_real_user_benchmark_v1_20261102; original user partitions and raw points unchanged.
selection: Select by received-pilot history and deterministic user-balanced hash order, not any CPOP/LABS/current-model result or whether power responds. Four strata: small0.5..2A change, short-held limit<=60s, other>=2A step, quiet-pilot background. Retain all selected cases including unresolved observations.
targets: Observed current/power change presence, onset bounds and return/end bounds when visible; plateau power summaries from explicitly reviewed native row ranges. No noise-free physical truth, causal participation, exact command-dispatch delay or sensor-fault labels.
precision: Bound transitions between original neighboring timestamps. Actual Pilot timestamp is received-limit observation; actual power change may be slightly before it. Never clip such timing to zero or fabricate finer data.
review: Assistant visually inspects original raw plots and source rows, no proposed model labels. This is a single assistant review, not independent human gold. Deterministic numerical consistency checks are not a second independent annotator. Export an unlabelled second-review packet separately.
safeguards: Current and power are same EVSE-reported channels and can be derived; agreement is consistency, not independent-meter fault truth. Isolated observations not erased or declared faulty. Unresolved not coded negative. Persist coverage and class counts.
training_gate: No production retraining from this small initial review. Establish label meaning, timing resolution, coverage and independent-review needs before a prospectively fixed training comparison. Original CPOP/LABS and beneficial production version remain preserved.
opensource: Label Studio official time-series template and Apache2 repository reviewed; export compatible raw JSON tasks/configuration for independent review without installing or starting a service. Static scientific plots use already installed matplotlib because bundled Python lacks that plotting capability.
